mainTopic: How objects are carried out on שבת: אגד כלי, normal versus unusual ways of carrying, carrying above ten טפחים, and carrying on the head
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a thief who drags a purse out to the רשות הרבים on שבת. The גמרא shows how the theft and the שבת violation can happen at the same moment: the purse holds metal bars and has no laces, or its laces are wrapped around it. Next, רבא and אביי disagree about whether a vessel binds the things inside it (אגד כלי). In another dispute, about carrying fruit out by hand or in a vessel, each of them seems to hold the other's view, so the גמרא switches the names. It then defends the switched version by distinguishing a hand held below three טפחים from one held above. A new משנה follows: carrying in normal ways, such as in the hand, the lap, or on the shoulders, makes one חייב, because that is how the בני קהת carried. Unusual ways make one פטור. In the גמרא, רבי אלעזר rules that carrying above ten טפחים is still חייב. The גמרא proves the בני קהת carried that high, first from the height of משה and the לויים, and then from the ארון. Finally, רב quoting רבי חייא discusses carrying a load on the head. After two challenges, the גמרא concludes that it is פטור, and that statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He could tear the purse and take the money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge. It asks why the thief is not already liable for theft while part of the purse is still inside, since he could tear it open and take the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if he wants, he can tear it open and take the money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing a challenge that began on the previous amud, in the case of a purse dragged out on שבת. It argues that the thief should already own the money before the purse is fully out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion needs the theft and the שבת violation to happen at the very same moment. But once part of the purse is in the רשות הרבים, the thief could rip it open and grab the coins. So the theft seems to come first, and the two would no longer happen together.

phrases.english: For if he wants, he can tear it and take (the money)!
phrases.notes: The end of a question that began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge earlier about the purse case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the theft and the שבת violation happen at the same moment in the purse case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The thief can reach the money once part of the purse is outside. So ownership, and liability for theft, should begin before the purse fully leaves the רשות היחיד.

steps.title: The purse holds long metal bars
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is one where the purse holds long metal bars, which cannot be taken out through a tear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about metal bars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the purse holds long bars of metal, not loose coins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Long bars cannot be pulled out of a small tear while part of the purse is still inside. So the thief does not gain the money until the whole purse is out. That keeps the theft and the שבת violation at the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: a bar or strip of metal

phrases.english: With metal bars.
phrases.notes: Long strips that cannot be slipped out early.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The purse holds coins that could be pulled out through a tear.
steps.terutzMaskana: The purse holds long metal bars that cannot come out until the whole purse is out.

steps.title: But a purse with laces opens at the mouth
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge: if the purse has laces, the thief could bring just the mouth outside, untie it, and take the money. Meanwhile the laces are still tied inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since there are laces, he can bring it out up to its mouth, untie it and take the money, while the laces are still tied inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer again. Even with metal bars, a purse with laces could be opened at its mouth once only the mouth is outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the opening reaches the רשות הרבים, the thief can untie it and remove the contents, so he would already be liable for theft. But the laces are still inside, so the purse is not fully out and the שבת violation has not happened yet. Once again the theft would come before the שבת violation.

keyTerms.meaning: laces or straps used to close a purse

phrases.english: And since there are laces,
he can bring it out up to its mouth
and untie and take (the contents),
while the laces are still tied inside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the metal-bars answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that metal bars keep the theft and the שבת violation together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The laces let the thief open the purse at its mouth. So he gets the money while part of the purse is still inside, and the two events split apart again.

steps.title: The purse has no laces
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: the case is a purse that has no laces.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where there are no laces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case further: the purse has no laces at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without laces there is no opening to untie. So the bars still cannot come out until the whole purse is outside.

phrases.english: Where there are no laces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The purse has laces that can be untied at its mouth.
steps.terutzMaskana: The purse has no laces, so it cannot be opened early.

steps.title: Or the laces are wrapped around the purse
steps.stepSummary: A second possible answer: the purse does have laces, but they are wound around the whole purse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it does have laces, but they are wrapped around it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the laces are wound around the body of the purse, bringing out only the mouth does not let the thief undo them. He still has to bring out the whole purse before he can get the money.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces an alternative answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The purse case works only when the thief cannot get at the money until the whole purse is out. That is the case of metal bars, with no laces or with laces wrapped around the purse.

phrases.english: And if you want, say that it does have (laces),
and they are wrapped around it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Laces always let the mouth be opened early.
steps.terutzMaskana: Laces wrapped around the purse cannot be undone from the mouth alone.

steps.title: רבא: a basket of mustard seeds makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits the משנה's exemption to a basket of large produce. If the basket is full of tiny mustard seeds, the person is liable. This shows רבא holds that a vessel does not bind its contents together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבא: The משנה taught the exemption only for a basket full of cucumbers and gourds. But if it is full of mustard seeds, he is liable. So he holds that being held together by a vessel does not count as being bound together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבא about a basket that is partly outside, which shares the logic of the previous discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Large cucumbers or gourds lying partly inside are not fully out, so he is exempt. Mustard seeds are tiny, so many of them are fully outside on their own, and he is liable for those. רבא does not let the basket tie the seeds to the part still inside, so in his view a vessel does not bind its contents (אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד).

keyTerms.meaning: they taught this only in the case of
being bound together by a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: Cucumbers in a basket are exempt because each one is partly inside. The argument here is only about tiny items that are completely outside but still sit in a basket that is partly inside.

phrases.english: And so said Rava:
They taught (the exemption) only
for a basket full of cucumbers and gourds,
but if it is full of mustard seeds, he is liable.
Evidently he holds
that binding by a vessel is not considered binding.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel dispute, linked by the word וכן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basket of mustard seeds partly outside makes him liable, because a vessel does not bind its contents (אגד כלי לא שמיה אגד).

steps.title: אביי: even mustard seeds are exempt
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees with רבא. Even a basket of mustard seeds is exempt, because the vessel binds its contents together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if it is full of mustard seeds, he is exempt. So he holds that being held together by a vessel does count as being bound together.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the opposite view about the same basket case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the basket ties all the seeds into one unit. Since part of the basket is still inside, none of the seeds count as fully taken out. That is the view that a vessel binds its contents (אגד כלי שמיה אגד).
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: a vessel does not bind (mustard seeds, liable). אביי: a vessel does bind (mustard seeds, exempt).

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even if it is full of mustard seeds, he is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא קָסָבַר אֶגֶד כְּלִי שְׁמֵיהּ אֶגֶד.
phrases.english: evidently he holds that binding by a vessel is considered binding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבא in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a basket of mustard seeds is exempt, because a vessel binds its contents (אגד כלי שמיה אגד).

steps.title: Each אמורא seems to hold the other's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that אביי later took רבא's position and רבא took אביי's. So each one's statements appear to contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי stood in רבא's position, and רבא stood in אביי's position. So there is a contradiction between אביי and אביי, and between רבא and רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a contradiction: אביי and רבא later exchanged positions, and another dispute of theirs clashes with their new views. The next step brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each אמורא holds the opposite view somewhere else, then each one contradicts himself. The גמרא states the problem here and shows where it comes from right after.

phrases.english: Abaye took up the position of Rava,
Rava took up the position of Abaye,
and one raises a contradiction from Abaye against Abaye,
and from Rava against Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how consistent the views in steps 6 and 7 are.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of אביי and רבא on אגד כלי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere each one seems to hold the opposite principle, so each contradicts himself.

steps.title: The source: carrying fruit out by hand or in a vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the other dispute. אביי says carrying fruit out in the hand makes one liable and in a vessel exempt; רבא says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: One who carries fruit out to the רשות הרבים — אביי says: by hand, liable; in a vessel, exempt. רבא says: by hand, exempt; in a vessel, liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source of the contradiction it just announced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is someone who stays inside and reaches out holding fruit, either in his hand or in a vessel. The clash is with the views they took after exchanging positions. אביי now holds that a vessel does not bind, yet here he exempts the vessel case. רבא now holds that a vessel does bind, yet here he makes the vessel case liable.

phrases.english: As it was stated:
One who carries fruit out to the public domain:
Abaye said: by hand, he is liable;
in a vessel, he is exempt.
And Rava said: by hand, he is exempt;
in a vessel, he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That אביי and רבא appear to switch positions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The אמוראי dispute about carrying fruit out by hand or in a vessel.

steps.title: Reverse the names: by hand, liable
steps.stepSummary: The answer: switch the names in the fruit dispute, so that רבא is the one who says carrying by hand makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: (רבא says) by hand, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by switching the names of the two speakers in the fruit dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא had exchanged views, so רבא now holds that a vessel binds its contents and אביי holds that it does not. After the switch, רבא says by hand liable (the hand is not bound to the body) and in a vessel exempt, which fits his new view. אביי says by hand exempt (the hand follows the body) and in a vessel liable, which fits his new view.

phrases.english: Reverse it: by hand, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in steps 8 and 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא holds that carrying by hand makes one liable, which matches his view on אגד כלי.

steps.title: The משנה says a hand reaching out is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reversed version from the משנה. There, when the homeowner reaches his hand outside and an object is taken from it or put into it, both people are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: If the homeowner stretched his hand outside, and the poor man took from it, or put something into it and he brought it in — both are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reversed ruling that carrying something out by hand makes one liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the homeowner's hand holding an object is in the רשות הרבים. Yet the object is not treated as properly carried out or put down there, so he is exempt. That seems to contradict a ruling that bringing fruit out in the hand makes one liable.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ,
phrases.english: The homeowner stretched his hand outside,
and the poor man took from it,
or put into it and (the homeowner) brought it in —
both are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reversed ruling in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that bringing fruit out by hand makes one liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts a case where an object rests in a hand stretched out into the רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Above three טפחים versus below three
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in the משנה the hand was higher than three טפחים off the ground. In the fruit case it was lower than three טפחים, where it counts as resting on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the hand was above three טפחים; here, it was below three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the two cases differ in how high the hand was held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anything within three טפחים of the ground is treated as if it were lying on the ground. So fruit held that low counts as put down in the רשות הרבים, and he is liable. In the משנה the hand was higher, so nothing counted as put down, and both are exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: After the names are switched, רבא is consistent: a holder, whether a vessel or a hand, does not bind its contents. Carrying out by hand makes one liable when the hand is below three טפחים, because that counts as resting on the ground.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that something within three טפחים of the ground counts as resting on the ground is used often in the laws of carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: There, it was above three (handbreadths);
here, it was below three.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לְמַעְלָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה הָכָא לְמַטָּה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hand reaching outside never makes one liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Below three טפחים the object counts as resting on the ground, so he is liable. Above three, he is exempt.

steps.title: Carrying in the normal ways makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that carrying out with either hand, in the lap, or on the shoulders makes one חייב, because this is how the בני קהת carried.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: One who carries out, whether in his right hand or his left hand, in his lap or on his shoulders, is liable, because this is how the sons of Kehat carried.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It lists the normal ways of carrying that make a person חייב for הוצאה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All מלאכות of שבת are learned from the משכן. The בני קהת carried the holy vessels of the משכן, so their style of carrying sets the standard for what counts as normal carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries out from one domain to another
His lap or the fold of his garment
Liable (here, liable to bring a קרבן חטאת)
The way the sons of קהת carried the משכן vessels

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for the whole sugya: carrying is measured against how the בני קהת carried in the desert.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who carries out, whether in his right hand
or in his left hand
in his lap or on his shoulders
is liable
for such was the carrying of the sons of Kehat

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצִיא, בֵּין בִּימִינוֹ בֵּין בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins. It moves on from the hand-height discussion in steps 8–12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normal carrying, whether with either hand, in the lap, or on the shoulders, makes one חייב, based on משא בני קהת.

steps.title: Carrying in unusual ways makes one exempt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists unusual ways of carrying, such as backhanded, with the foot, mouth, elbow, ear, hair, an upside-down belt, the cloak hem, or a shoe. For all of these one is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Backhanded, with his foot, with his mouth or elbow, with his ear or hair, with his belt whose opening faces down, between his belt and his cloak, with the hem of his cloak, with his shoe or sandal: he is exempt, because he did not carry out the way people carry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the opposite side. It lists strange ways of carrying that do not make a person חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is one simple principle: the Torah only makes you חייב for a מלאכה done the normal way. These methods are not how people usually carry things, so there is no חיוב חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Backhanded, in an unusual and awkward manner
A hollow belt used as a money pouch
Exempt (from a קרבן; usually still forbidden מדרבנן)

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does not mean you are allowed to do it. It means there is no Torah-level חיוב, but it is still forbidden.

phrases.english: backhandedly, with his foot
with his mouth or with his elbow
with his ear or with his hair
or with his belt whose opening faces downward
between his belt and his cloak
or with the hem of his cloak
with his shoe, with his sandal
is exempt
for he did not carry out in the manner of those who carry

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second half of the same משנה. It gives the exempt cases that contrast with step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unusual methods of carrying make one פטור, because they are not כדרך המוציאין.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: carrying above ten handbreadths is still liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that carrying a load out above ten טפחים makes one חייב, because the בני קהת carried that high.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רבי אלעזר said: One who carries out a load above ten handbreadths is liable, because this is how the sons of Kehat carried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבי אלעזר's new rule. A load carried high up, more than ten טפחים off the ground, still counts as carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, the רשות הרבים only goes up to ten טפחים, so something high above might seem to be outside the domain. רבי אלעזר says it still counts, because the בני קהת themselves carried their loads that high.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten handbreadths, the normal height limit of a domain

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shapes what follows. The rest of this passage works to prove that the בני קהת really carried above ten טפחים.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabbi Elazar said
One who carries out a load
above ten handbreadths
is liable, for such was the carrying of the sons of Kehat

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַמּוֹצִיא מַשּׂאוֹי לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This uses the משנה's reasoning of משא בני קהת and applies it to a new question: carrying at a height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying a load above ten טפחים is חייב, based on משא בני קהת.

steps.title: How do we know the sons of Kehat carried that high?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the בני קהת carried their loads above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the carrying of the sons of Kehat, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of רבי אלעזר's claim. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's rule depends completely on a fact about history: that the בני קהת carried high. The גמרא wants to see where that fact comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And the carrying of the sons of Kehat, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This asks for the source of the fact that step 15 relies on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the בני קהת carried their loads above ten טפחים.

steps.title: The altar is compared to the Tabernacle: ten cubits
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק places the מזבח next to the משכן. This teaches that just as the משכן was ten אמות, so was the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'around the Tabernacle and the altar.' The verse compares the altar to the Tabernacle: just as the Tabernacle was ten cubits, so too the altar was ten cubits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a הקש, a comparison between two things the פסוק mentions together. Because the משכן and the מזבח are mentioned side by side, the מזבח gets the same height of ten אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first building block. The מזבח that the לויים carried was very tall, ten אמות. The גמרא still needs to show how high off the ground it was carried, so it asks a further question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, through a הֶקֵּשׁ (two things placed side by side in a פסוק)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'around the Tabernacle and the altar'
it compares the altar to the Tabernacle
just as the Tabernacle was ten cubits
so too the altar was ten cubits

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers step 16 by connecting the height of the מזבח to the משכן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through a הקש, the מזבח is ten אמות, just like the משכן.

steps.title: How do we know about the Tabernacle itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source about the משכן itself, which the comparison in step 17 relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Tabernacle itself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the משכן, because the answer in step 17 depended on it. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 17 is only as strong as what we know about the משכן. So the גמרא now asks for the source of that, which will lead to a proof about how tall the לויים were.

phrases.english: And the Tabernacle itself, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This goes one step deeper, asking about the basis of the comparison in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the משכן's height and how high it was carried.

steps.title: Moses spread the tent, so the Levites were ten cubits tall
steps.stepSummary: The קרשים were ten אמות tall, and משה spread the אהל over them by himself. So the לויים were ten אמות tall. Since a load on poles hangs one-third above the carrier and two-thirds below, the מזבח was carried very high.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Ten cubits is the length of a board,' and it is written: 'He spread the tent over the Tabernacle,' and רב said: Moses our teacher spread it. From here you learn that the Levites were ten cubits tall. And we have a tradition that any load carried on poles is one-third above and two-thirds below. It turns out that it was carried very high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts together two פסוקים, a statement of רב, and a tradition. Together they show that the לויים carried loads far above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the chain. The boards were ten אמות tall, and משה spread the cover over them alone, so he must have been ten אמות tall, and the other לויים were assumed to be the same height. A ten-אמה מזבח hanging two-thirds below such a tall carrier still had its bottom far off the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: A board of the משכן wall
The Levites, who carried the משכן

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Ten cubits is the length of a board'
and it is written: 'And he spread the tent over the Tabernacle'
and Rav said: Moses our teacher spread it
from here you learn
that the height of the Levites was ten cubits
And we have a tradition that any load
that is carried on poles
one-third is above
and two-thirds are below
it turns out that it was raised very high

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers step 18 and completes the first proof for רבי אלעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה, and so the לויים, were ten אמות tall. With the tradition about poles (one-third above, two-thirds below), the מזבח was carried far above ten טפחים.

steps.title: Second proof: from the Ark
steps.stepSummary: Another way to prove it: the ארון was nine טפחים and the כפורת one טפח, ten in total. Carried with one-third above and two-thirds below, its bottom was above ten טפחים from the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you wish, say: from the Ark. For the Master said: the Ark was nine handbreadths and the cover one handbreadth, making ten. And we have a tradition that any load carried on poles is one-third above and two-thirds below. It turns out that it stood above ten handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second, different proof that the בני קהת carried above ten טפחים. This one uses the ארון and does not need the לויים to be giants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proof works even if the לויים were of normal height. The ארון with its כפורת was only ten טפחים tall, so even with two-thirds of it hanging below the carriers' shoulders, its bottom was still higher than ten טפחים off the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: from the Ark

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָר: אָרוֹן תִּשְׁעָה וְכַפּוֹרֶת טֶפַח
phrases.english: for the Master said: the Ark was nine and the cover one handbreadth
here there are ten
And we have a tradition that any load carried on poles
one-third is above and two-thirds below
it turns out that it stood above ten

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second answer to step 16. It replaces the proof from the height of the לויים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten-טפח ארון, carried on poles, had its bottom above ten טפחים from the ground.

steps.title: Why not just learn it from Moses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the second proof was needed. Why not simply rely on the first proof from משה's height?
steps.simpleTranslation: And let us learn it from Moses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the second proof. The proof from משה seemed to work, so why bring the ארון? The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first proof were strong enough, there would be no reason for an איבעית אימא. The question forces the גמרא to show a weak point in the proof from משה.

phrases.english: And let us learn it from Moses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This questions why step 20's alternative proof was needed, given step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the second proof (the ארון) in step 20
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The proof from משה's height already showed high carrying, so a second proof seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Moses was different: the Shechinah rests only on the tall
steps.stepSummary: משה may have been special. The שכינה only rests on someone wise, strong, wealthy, and tall, so the other לויים may not have been as tall as he was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps Moses was different, for the Master said: The Divine Presence rests only on one who is wise, mighty, wealthy, and tall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we cannot assume all the לויים were as tall as משה. משה was unusual, so the ארון proof was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from משה assumed that the other לויים were his height. But משה was a נביא, and the שכינה rests only on a tall person, so his height may have been unique to him. That weakens the first proof, and the ארון proof does not depend on anyone's height.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: carrying above ten טפחים is חייב, like the בני קהת. The best proof is the ארון, which was carried with its bottom above ten טפחים. The proof from משה's height is weaker, because משה was unique.

phrases.english: Perhaps Moses was different
for the Master said: the Divine Presence does not rest
except upon one who is wise, mighty
wealthy, and tall

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers step 21 by showing why the proof from משה could not stand alone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out a weak point in the first proof (the unusual height of one person cannot be applied to everyone)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's height of ten אמות tells us the height of all the לויים.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה was uniquely tall because the שכינה rested on him, so the proof from the ארון is needed.

steps.title: Carrying a load on the head makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoting רבי חייא, rules that carrying a load on one's head on שבת makes a person חייב חטאת, because the people of הוצל carry that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said in the name of רבי חייא: Someone who carries a load out on שבת on his head must bring a חטאת, because the people of הוצל carry like that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. Carrying on your head counts as a real, normal way of carrying, so it breaks שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is only חייב for carrying on שבת if he carries in a normal way. רבי חייא's reason is that a whole town, הוצל, normally carries loads on their heads. So he treats head-carrying as normal.

keyTerms.meaning: Must bring a sin-offering, meaning he did a real מלאכה by mistake
The people of הוצל, a town in Bavel

phrases.english: Rav said in the name of Rabbi Ḥiyya:
One who carries out a burden on Shabbat on his head
is liable to a sin-offering,
since the people of Hotzal do so.
phrases.notes: They normally carried loads on their heads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about unusual ways of carrying, after the discussion of the משכן's height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying a load on the head on שבת is חייב חטאת, because the people of הוצל carry this way.

steps.title: One town is not most of the world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason. The people of הוצל are not the majority of the world, so their habit cannot make head-carrying normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the people of הוצל most of the world?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי חייא's reason. One small town's habit does not decide what is normal for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a way of carrying is "normal" depends on how most people carry. Since most people do not carry loads on their heads, the habit of הוצל should not make it normal.

keyTerms.meaning: Most of the world, the majority of people

phrases.english: And are the people of Hotzal the majority of the world?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason "שכן אנשי הוצל עושין כן"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What counts as normal is decided by most people, and one town is not most people.

steps.title: The ruling applies only to a person from הוצל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי חייא's ruling. It only applies to someone from הוצל, since in his town head-carrying is normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this: רב said in the name of רבי חייא: A person from הוצל who carried a load out on his head on שבת is חייב, because the people of his town carry like that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ruling by making it narrower. Only a person from הוצל is חייב, not everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "אי איתמר הכי איתמר" means the original wording must have been wrong, and here is the correct version. Now the ruling does not claim that head-carrying is normal for the whole world. It only says it is normal for people of that town.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said, which corrects the wording of a ruling

steps.confusionAlert: "אי איתמר הכי איתמר" does not mean רבי חייא changed his mind. It means the גמרא is correcting how his statement was reported.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated as follows:
Rav said in the name of Rabbi Ḥiyya:
One of the people of Hotzal
who carried out a burden on his head on Shabbat
is liable,
since the people of his city do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by limiting the ruling to people from הוצל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the ruling to make it narrower
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Head-carrying is normal for everyone because הוצל does it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Head-carrying is only normal for, and only makes liable, a person from הוצל.

steps.title: His town's habit is outweighed by everyone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. Even a person from הוצל should follow what everyone else does, so his town's habit should not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But his way of thinking should be cancelled out by all other people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the narrower version too. Even for a person from הוצל, what is normal should be judged by the rest of the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that an individual's unusual habit is "בטל", cancelled out, by how all people behave. So the habit of one town does not turn head-carrying into normal carrying, even for the people of that town.

keyTerms.meaning: His way of thinking should be cancelled out

phrases.english: But let his intention be nullified relative to that of all people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reworded ruling from step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The narrower version: a person from הוצל is חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small group's unusual habit is cancelled out by how most people behave, so it never counts as normal.

steps.title: Final version: carrying on the head is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ruling a second time. It must have said the opposite: someone who carries a load on his head is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if this was said, it was said like this: Someone who carries a load out on his head is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: After both versions were challenged, the גמרא concludes that the ruling really said the opposite. Carrying on the head is פטור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both challenges showed that head-carrying is not a normal way of carrying for the world. So it is an unusual way of carrying, and a person is פטור from a חטאת. This now fits the rule that what is normal is decided by most people.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt, not liable to a חטאת

steps.whatToRemember: What counts as a "normal" way of carrying is decided by most people. Most people do not carry loads on their heads, so it is פטור, even though הוצל carries that way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that one town's or one person's unusual habit does not change what counts as normal carrying in הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was stated, it was stated as follows:
One who carries out a burden on his head is exempt,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by reversing the ruling to פטור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the ruling to say the opposite
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A person from הוצל who carries on his head is חייב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Anyone who carries a load on his head is פטור.
